paths.description: Homepage and global chrome, representing landing, navigation, consent and promotional modules. Excludes personalized signed-in content.
Search results for “headphones”, representing listing, filtering and product discovery.
Representative product detail page, covering content, pricing, buying controls, metadata and partial module failures.
Anonymous empty basket, representing cart state and recovery/next actions.
Recorded product-to-basket journey: decline cookies, add representative item, verify basket state.
Public sign-in entry, representing account authentication and autofill/passkey affordances. Credentials and post-auth checkout were intentionally not covered.

findings.summary: The storefront ignores the user’s dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: Under emulated dark mode the page body remained rgb(255,255,255), text remained dark, color-scheme was normal, and the preference screenshot stayed light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() for all core surfaces.

findings.summary: Route and state changes are abrupt rather than transition-aware.
findings.evidence: The four-route CSS/DOM probes found no view-transition declarations, while navigation between search, product and basket is a primary journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions with a reduced-motion-safe fallback for stable shared elements.

findings.summary: Carousel-like and overlay interactions rely on legacy custom controls rather than platform-native gesture primitives.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show horizontal card rails and custom overlays; probes found no scroll-snap/modern declarative gesture signal and 26-44 custom role dialogs per route.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-snap and overscroll behavior for rails, and native top-layer primitives for gestures and overlays.

findings.summary: The large site chrome does not adapt to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The homepage screenshot shows two persistent navigation rows; CSS probes found no scroll-state or scroll-timeline technique on any representative route.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query or a compact sticky header after scrolling.

findings.summary: Menus and popovers use custom positioned role-dialog structures without CSS anchor positioning.
findings.evidence: Probes found 26-44 role=dialog elements, zero native dialogs/popovers, and no anchor-name, position-anchor or position-try declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate transient menus to popover plus CSS anchor positioning and fallback positions.

findings.summary: Two load-time interruptions obscure shopping content.
findings.evidence: The first desktop capture shows a large cookie-consent layer covering the lower half of the viewport while a delivery-address popover covers the hero; the mobile capture also starts with the delivery overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-preserving consent surface and defer the delivery prompt until location is needed.

findings.summary: Overlays are built from custom role dialogs rather than native dialog or popover primitives.
findings.evidence: Across the representative pages probes counted 26-44 role dialogs but zero dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal consent and popover for transient menus, retaining declarative light-dismiss and focus behavior.

findings.summary: Dense navigation, promotions, badges and duplicated panels crowd the core content.
findings.evidence: The homepage first viewport is dominated by two navigation bars, a campaign banner and four competing promotional cards; the product probe exposed 14 h1 elements and repeated sustainability/error panels.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce duplicated modules and visual framing, and prioritize one clear content hierarchy per template.

findings.summary: The desktop storefront is scaled down instead of reflowing at a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout reported no viewport meta, a 1000 px layout viewport and 640 px horizontal overflow on the homepage; all four page probes reported viewport=null.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid width=device-width viewport declaration and ship layouts that reflow intrinsically at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Reusable cards and commerce panels do not demonstrate container-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: Representative probes found no @container rules in authored inline styles and mobile screenshots show desktop grids scaled to fit rather than components reorganized for their available space.
findings.suggestedFix: Use size container queries for product cards, buying panels and promotional modules.

findings.summary: Many controls are too small for touch and some keyboard focus indicators are absent.
findings.evidence: The probes counted 45/171 small targets on home, 97/247 on search and 176/409 on product; Lighthouse failed target-size, and several focused shortcut/search controls had no outline or shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24 by 24 CSS px target space, prefer 44 px for primary controls, and guarantee visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: Partial product failures are exposed without useful recovery actions.
findings.evidence: The product DOM contains repeated “Sorry, there was a problem” and “Issue loading the information” headings, while the captured product view provides no adjacent retry control.
findings.suggestedFix: Pair every failed module with concise state text and a retry, reload, or continue-without-it action.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is well outside the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 6.6 s, LCP 18.1 s, Speed Index 6.6 s and performance 0.56; the independent trace measured LCP 3.05 s under a lighter run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reduce initial request competition and defer noncritical modules.

findings.summary: The basket shifts visibly during load.
findings.evidence: The 360 px basket layout observer measured CLS 0.1104 from two shifts, exceeding the good <=0.1 threshold; 39 of 40 homepage images lacked both dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image and dynamic-module space with dimensions or aspect-ratio and keep late banners out of existing flow.

findings.summary: The initial page has a heavy, render-blocking network dependency shape.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 289 requests and 4.35 MB transferred, including five parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets, 21 fonts and 219 images; Lighthouse LCP was 18.1 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical styles, subset fonts, lazy-load offscreen images and shorten the LCP dependency chain.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped JavaScript and CSS are unused on the initial view.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 642 KiB unused JavaScript and 207 KiB unused CSS, including a 590 KiB WAF challenge script and feature bundles with 60-100% waste.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by template and interaction, conditionally load optional cards, and remove duplicated legacy assets.

findings.summary: Accessible semantics are inconsistent on complex product and search surfaces.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed aria-allowed-attr and label-content-name-mismatch; the product probe found 35 img elements without alt and the search probe found one.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct role/ARIA combinations, align visible and accessible names, and provide meaningful or empty alt attributes.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is malformed on key templates.
findings.evidence: The product page exposed 14 h1 elements, search had no main landmark, and focused search/shortcut controls sometimes had neither outline nor box-shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one page h1, a sequential heading hierarchy, one main landmark, and consistent :focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: Narrow-screen text is rendered as tiny desktop content.
findings.evidence: At 360 px, search and product pages are 1000 px desktop layouts scaled to 0.36; product descriptions and controls are visibly too small for comfortable reading.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow content at the device width and use fluid type and line lengths rather than page-wide scale-down.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow and touch-target support fail the inclusive baseline.
findings.evidence: All representative page probes lacked a viewport meta declaration; Lighthouse failed target-size and the mobile screenshots show desktop-scale layouts.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a scalable viewport, reflow at 320-400 px widths, and increase target size/spacing without disabling zoom.

findings.summary: The homepage logs a production console error.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a console.error for a late-loading Mash module from an Amazon JavaScript asset.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the late module dependency race or downgrade expected telemetry to a non-error channel after handling it.

findings.summary: Image sizing and document assets are not consistently sound.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 39/40 images without dimensions, 37 legacy-format images and two oversized images; Lighthouse also failed image aspect ratio and low-resolution image audits.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic dimensions, preserve aspect ratios, and serve responsive modern image candidates.

findings.summary: Deprecated API use remains in production.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecated-API warning and reduced the best-practices score to 0.69.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the deprecated API with its Baseline-supported platform equivalent and keep deprecation monitoring in CI.

findings.summary: Search and basket templates omit meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: The route probes found a descriptive title on all pages but description=null on search results and basket.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate unique descriptions for public listing templates; keep private basket routes intentionally excluded from indexing.

findings.summary: The site is neither consistently crawlable nor mobile-friendly.
findings.evidence: The homepage had five javascript: links, product had 106, Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors, and every representative template lacked a viewport meta declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations for navigation and add a device-width viewport with responsive reflow.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are inconsistent across localized and listing pages.
findings.evidence: Home and product had canonicals, but search had no canonical; no representative page exposed hreflang despite German and English variants. robots.txt itself was valid.
findings.suggestedFix: Add stable canonicals to public listings and reciprocal hreflang for localized variants.

findings.summary: Product pages lack structured product and social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The product probe found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph tags despite a visible price, availability, ratings and product identity.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit accurate schema.org Product/Offer JSON-LD plus Open Graph metadata that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Core transport defenses and cookie attributes are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but the headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS or nosniff; seven of nine cookies were flagged, including three non-Secure cookies and auth-like session identifiers without HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, a restrictive CSP and nosniff, and review every cookie for Secure, HttpOnly and least-permissive SameSite.

findings.summary: The anonymous homepage has a large telemetry and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Before consent, HAR saw 282 cross-origin requests and 4.13 MB cross-origin transfer; the consent text names 129 advertising partners and Amazon telemetry origins were active.
findings.suggestedFix: Block nonessential collection until consent, reduce event volume, batch telemetry and document each third-party purpose.

findings.summary: The sign-in entry point is password-oriented and exposes no passkey option.
findings.evidence: The valid sign-in probe found username autocomplete but no passkey text, no WebAuthn signal, and a password field with no autocomplete token; no permission prompt appeared on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey/WebAuthn sign-in and set current-password autocomplete only as a fallback path.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The main response exposed no frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to missing CSP/HSTS; no frame-ancestors policy could be found.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and appropriate origin isolation/Trusted Types controls.

findings.summary: The public homepage is effectively unavailable to a non-JavaScript generic crawler.
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetched HTTP 202 with only 2,007 raw bytes: 1% content coverage, no raw title or description, and isJsShell=true; the product page was materially better at 61% coverage.
findings.suggestedFix: Return meaningful server-rendered navigation and homepage content before enhancement, including through bot/WAF handling.

findings.summary: Custom overlays and asynchronously loaded product modules are fragile.
findings.evidence: Representative probes found 26-44 role dialogs with no native top-layer primitives, while the product DOM contained repeated issue-loading states.
findings.suggestedFix: Use resilient native top-layer primitives, position fallbacks and conditional async loading with stable fallback content.

findings.summary: Network-backed product module failures do not present actionable recovery.
findings.evidence: The product page repeatedly rendered “Sorry, there was a problem” and “Issue loading the information” without an adjacent retry control in the captured state.
findings.suggestedFix: Add bounded timeouts and explicit Retry/Continue actions while preserving the product and basket context.

findings.summary: Localized pages rely overwhelmingly on physical CSS and mix languages within the product experience.
findings.evidence: html lang=en-gb was valid, but probes found hundreds of left/right declarations and almost no logical-property usage; the English product route contains multiple German h1 sections.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical properties and mark language changes on translated product modules.

findings.summary: Consent choices are visually asymmetric and interrupt the task.
findings.evidence: The cookie layer gives Accept a filled yellow primary style while Decline is a gray outline, covers half the desktop viewport, and describes sharing with 129 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Give accept and reject equal visual weight, shorten the initial explanation, and keep granular controls one step away.

findings.summary: Authentication autofill metadata is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The sign-in email uses autocomplete=username, but the password input has an empty autocomplete value and no passkey path is exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use current-password for the password fallback and support passkeys; retain correct username metadata.

findings.summary: The image estate is dominated by legacy, unreserved and non-responsive assets.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 37/40 legacy formats, 39 missing dimensions, 26 missing srcset and 22 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP responsive candidates, reserve dimensions and lazy-load noncritical imagery.

findings.summary: The initial view performs disproportionate network and code work.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 289 requests and 4.35 MB; Lighthouse found 642 KiB unused JS and 207 KiB unused CSS, while telemetry endpoints made repeated background requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load modules, batch/deprioritize telemetry and remove work with no first-view user value.

findings.summary: Third-party, font and media costs are not proportionate to the first view.
findings.evidence: HAR attributed 4.13 MB to cross-origin resources, including 2.25 MB images and 735 KB across 21 fonts; 282 of 289 requests were cross-origin by host.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route budget, reduce font variants, defer offscreen media and hold third-party work behind consent and interaction.

findings.summary: The commerce surface is deliberately opaque to agents and exposes no structured action interface.
findings.evidence: robots.txt disallows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User and many other agents; probes found no WebMCP, product JSON-LD or agentic tool registration.
findings.suggestedFix: For approved agents, expose scoped WebMCP commerce tools and machine-readable product/actions with explicit authorization boundaries.
